subject: Private IaC: module encapsulation + CI gate proposal
content:
From: Sam Rios <s.rios@acme-analytics.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: dependency isolation questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We have two outstanding concerns from our infra team before we sign off on the on-prem contract:

1) Module dependency churn: our audit team flagged that some Terraform modules in the repository reach across VPC and host-level boundaries (e.g., vpc subnet creation + host ACLs in the same module). That makes rollbacks risky.
2) CI gating: we need stronger per-module gating so changes to network/egress modules run a stricter test matrix and require an approver from our security team.

Can you share an opinionated plan for:
- How Redwood intends to enforce module boundaries (Terraform + Helm chart layering + Ansible roles)
- What CI gate checks (unit, plan, drift simulation, network policy tests) you'll require before merge to main

Attaching a quick dependency matrix we generated that highlights three modules of concern.

attachment: priv-iac-dep-matrix.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Sam

--
Sam Rios
SRE, Acme Analytics

Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: dependency isolation questions

Team — forwarding Acme's matrix and asks. They want a proposal that clearly separates: infra-network (VPC + routing), host-provision (baremetal/k8s nodes), and platform-config (Helm releases, app overlays). Key constraints:
- No Terraform module should both create a VPC and mutate per-host firewall rules.
- Helm charts must avoid embedding cluster-level resource creation (e.g., clusterroles, networkpolicies that are not namespaced) unless explicitly approved.

Please propose the minimal CI gating steps that meet their audit bar and are feasible in our GitLab/Argo workflow. I'm looking for a short, actionable plan by EOD tomorrow.

Jonas

-----

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: dependency isolation questions

Thanks Jonah — quick proposal below. I focused on minimal disruption to current modules.

Proposal (summary):
- Module boundaries
  - Split any module touching both networking and host-level config into two modules: vpc-* (networking only) and host-* (host provisioning, security groups, ACLs).
  - Introduce a lightweight \"interface\" terraform module (tf-module-interface) that exports outputs consumed by downstream modules (subnet ids, route table ids) to avoid cross-module mutability.
- Helm/Ansible
  - Helm charts: enforce namespace-only installs for application charts. Charts that need cluster-scoped resources will be placed under a dedicated repo (cluster-ops) and require explicit signoff.
  - Ansible roles: separate host prep vs app deploy roles; keep secrets retrieval out of role logic and use vault-agent sidecar pattern.
- CI gating
  - Pre-merge pipeline: terraform validate, tflint, plan (with planfile upload to MR for reviewers), helm lint, ansible-lint. Reject MR if plan diffs include cluster-scoped resources for app charts.
  - Staging gate: run a constrained apply in a sandbox (feature branch environment) using ephemeral infra where feasible; run a small connectivity matrix (control-plane -> app namespace connectivity, egress to allowed CIDRs).
  - Security gate: any changes touching network modules (vpc-*, route-*, firewall-*) must be manually approved by a security owner and pass a network-policy simulation (we can run Calico policy simulator).
- Observability and traceability
  - Record module manifest and module interface versions in release artifact (module-manifest.json).
  - Require module tagging and sign-off (owner approvals tracked in MR).

Action items:
- I'll draft a concise CI gating MR template and a small demo sandbox pipeline.
- Need input from Grace/Lau ra on feasibility for the sandbox infra run.

-karthik

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: dependency isolation questions

Karthik — solid. A couple of operational notes from the runtime team:

- Sandbox applies: run them on prewarmed lightweight nodes with strict quotas to avoid cost surprises. Use policies to limit sequence lengths (for model-serving workloads) — joking, ignore that last line.
- For network policy simulation we already have a short script that runs synthetic flows and verifies ACL rules; I'll wire that into the staging gate.
- One gap: artifact provenance. We should require signed module artifacts (terraform module registry signed objects) as part of the release pipeline to meet Acme's audit requirement.

I volunteer to prototype the network policy simulation integration into the CI job.

-grace

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sam Rios <s.rios@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC: module encapsulation + CI gate proposal

Sam/Priya — apologies for the delay, and thanks for the clear asks. We've run the proposal past our CI and security leads and the attached short doc captures the agreed gating behavior. Highlights:

- Terraform module split: we identified 4 modules in your matrix that need carving out. Recommended pattern: vpc-* (network only) + host-* (provisioning + firewall attachment) with tf-module-interface for outputs.
- CI jobs added to MR template:
  - terraform/validate + tflint (fast fail)
  - terraform/plan (planfile uploaded, diff scanned for cluster-scoped resource changes)
  - sandbox-apply (ephemeral apply + smoke tests)
  - network-sim (synthetic flow tests)
  - artifact-signature-check (verify module artifact signatures)
- Approval policy:
  - Network modules require 2 approvers: one infra owner + one security approver (Acme can list their approvers in CODEOWNERS).

Attachments: ci-gating-proposal.md, tf-module-boundaries.png

Next steps:
1) We will open a joint MR in your upstream repo with the module-splits suggested.
2) Grace will add the network-sim CI job and prod a demo run for you to review.
3) Karthik will submit the MR template and sandbox pipeline jobs.

If that sounds right, can you confirm owners for review (who will be the security approvers on your side)?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Eng
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Sam Rios <s.rios@acme-analytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC: module encapsulation + CI gate proposal

Thanks, Laura — this looks good. We can assign Priya and me as the Acme approvers for network modules. Please go ahead with the MR splits and CI additions.

A couple of small asks before we close the loop:
- In the sandbox-apply job, can you capture a tarball with the plan outputs and network-sim logs and attach them to the MR for audit?
- Can the artifact-signature-check job publish a short JSON blob with the verified module digests and signer IDs to a secure URL (we'll consume that for our compliance pipeline)?

If you can include those, we can sign off on the changes and proceed with the contract finalization.

—Sam
SRE, Acme Analytics
